title: The dance of the forces
blurb: Why most things on a chart of mass and size fall on one diagonal: electromagnetism against gravity, then the strong force and fusion, then the weak force, from a stick to a neutron star, and the strangest of objects, a black hole.

segments.from: But the speed of light works

_note: The forces Short from the second take (rec75, 2026-11-18): its own opening, recorded for it ('If you try to map every single thing that exists in a chart of mass and size…', the author at 3:04: 'now I'm going to rerecord this, but only for the intro of the dance of forces'), then from 'everything in our universe is a delicate dance' to 'That's when the strangest of objects is born, a black hole' (the author at 13:10: 'so that's where the short ends'). Left out to fit under 3:00 (it came to 3:31 whole): the chemical bonds, gravity against electromagnetism and the round worlds, 'Get massive enough…', the tug of war, why the giant planets' core changes ('These planets are massive…'), the small stars' end, the neutrons packed shoulder to shoulder and held by gravity, the heavy elements, and 'half the speed of light'; escape velocity comes in on '…escape velocity, the speed you need to win the tug of war against an object's gravity'.
